title: Why CSA Scores Should Be Treated Like a Team Sport
summary: Find out why CSA scores matter, and why everyone - whether owner, driver or dispatcher - plays a central role.
body_text: Every carrier with a Department of Transportation (DOT) number receives an ongoing and updated safety score as part of the Compliance, Safety, Accountability (CSA) program. These safety scores indicate the success of that carrier, impacting the way drivers, inspectors, shippers, receivers, brokers, and more, interact with them. This article serves as a guide to what CSA scores are, how they are measured, why they matter, and ways to lower them. CSA scores are of utmost importance to carriers, and as we'll see, they should be treated like a team sport, where everyone associated with a particular carrier - whether driver or employee - must play a central role in achieving an optimal score to not only win the game, but the entire championship. What Is a CSA Score? The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) manages the CSA (Compliance, Safety, Accountability) program, all under the DOT umbrella. The intent of the program is to improve safety on the roads through preventing accidents. It's also a way to identify carriers with higher risks for accidents by holding them accountable for their own actions. The CSA program focuses on data using a three-prong approach: Measure. It starts with the Safety Measurement System (SMS) . This involves the data evaluations from inspections, investigations, and accident reports. Intervene. Then, when needed, there are Interventions. This involves formal processes to highlight and monitor carriers that have poor scores with the intent to help the carriers improve. Evaluate. Finally, there is the Safety and Fitness Determination (SFD) rating system. Not all carriers end up with a SFD score and no rating in this area generally is not a problem. The focus of this article is on the first part - the SMS (Safety Measurement System) - where a carrier and driver's actions have the most direct impact. Just like in golf, the lower the CSA score, the better. And when a carrier has a low CSA score, there is much less of a need to be concerned about the intervention and evaluation parts. However, if a carrier needs improvement with its SMS, those two parts are critical in minimizing the safety risk that fleet - all of its drivers - poses to everyone on the road. How are CSA Scores Measured? The SMS (Safety Measurement System) uses data from inspections, investigations, and accident reports to measure seven Behavior Analysis and Safety Improvement Categories (BASICs) : The seven BASICs of safety Unsafe Driving : Actions while driving such as speeding, texting, not wearing a seatbelt, improper lane changes, etc. Hours-of-Service (HOS) Compliance : Failing to adhere to drive-time mandates and/or proper logging of that time. Driver Fitness : How fit a driver is (CDL, medical certificates, driving records, etc) Vehicle Maintenance : The condition of your equipment through parts such as tires, brakes, lights, cargo securement, and other, as evaluated through pre- and post-trip inspections, vehicle defects, and repairs. Crash Indicator : Frequency and severity of crashes (defined as when a fatality or injury occurs, or when the vehicle requires transportation from the scene). Controlled Substances / Alcohol : Driving under the influence of alcohol (including having alcoholic beverages in the cab) or illegal drugs (and includes the abuse of prescription or over-the-counter medications). Hazardous Material Compliance : The handling of a hazmat load (packaging, marking, attendance, etc). Each month, the SMS compiles data safety incidents, inspections and investigations that occurred over the past two years. The data from all BASIC categories gets matched up to each carrier's DOT number, ultimately assigning points based on the violation and severity. These points then factor into a unique safety rating - somewhere on a percentile scale between 0-100 - which gets ranked both against the carrier's individual actions as well as against the carrier's peers (other carriers of similar truck and driver size). As mentioned, the lower the score - the closer to 0 - the better. Each time a violation is issued, it negatively affects that carrier‚Äôs score by adding points to it. Even if you just get a warning, rather than an actual ticket, you still receive the same amount of CSA points. Each individual violation is scored between 1-10, depending on the severity of the violation. For instance, an Unsafe Driving speeding violation of 15 miles over the limit impacts the score at a higher rate (10 points) than one for 11-14 miles over the limit (7 points). Or, an HOS Compliance violation for falsification of or inaccurate information on your record duty of status impacts it higher (7 points) than a violation for failing to assume or decline unassigned driving time (5 points). But, it doesn't stop there, because any violation is also weighed based on the timeframe of when it occurred (the more recent, the higher the points). Specifically, violations that happened within: 0-6 months get multiplied by three 6-12 months get multiplied by two 12-24 months get counted only once When a carrier's rating in a BASIC area is above the CSA threshold, then the carrier is subject to additional scrutiny, and possibly, intervention. If a carrier's rating is above the threshold in more than one BASIC area, then the additional scrutiny and intervention is magnified. While some carriers may have differences on how the SMS program was designed and is administered, what is clear is carriers with BASIC scores above the threshold have more accidents than carriers with BASIC scores below the threshold. DataQs is a system that allows you to challenge a violation if you feel it is unwarranted or unjustified. It should be noted that it is not easy to successfully challenge a violation. When it does happen, it's often because there is physical evidence such as a dashcam. It should also be noted that the ability to challenge a violation only applies to citations. You cannot challenge a warning (meaning that warnings always count toward your CSA score). Why Do CSA Scores Matter? A carrier's ratings for all BASIC categories above are available to the public with the exception of the Crash Indicator and Hazardous Material Compliance categories. CSA scores matter greatly. Here are a few of the main reasons why it is in your best interest to do everything possible to keep them low: Fewer inspections. High scores indicate a carrier is at greater risk for being involved in accidents, which lead to more inspections. This can be a slippery slope, resulting in additional violations, including a higher score and possibly even an out-of-service order, interventions, and more. With a low score, you are not subject to the same level of scrutiny. Better business opportunities. Many shippers and customers use CSA scores to evaluate carriers.‚ÄúIf you have a bad score, there are a lot of shippers and other customers won't work with you,‚Äù Charles, DOT Compliance and Safety Manager, explains. The criteria by which they will or will not do business with a carrier varies, but each has their own threshold, and oftentimes, when a score hits that threshold, they pass. Having a low CSA score will enable you to attract more opportunities and often at higher rates. Lower insurance costs. Financially, good CSA scores can help carriers get better insurance rates. The lower scores indicate lower risks of accidents and that translates into lower rates. Attract good talent to the fleet. Quality drivers, who understand how CSA scores impact their ability to keep moving and make money, are also attracted to carriers with good scores. Why are CSA Scores Like a Team Sport? While individual drivers do not receive individual CSA scores, every single action of the driver has the potential to impact the carrier's CSA score. This is just the same as in sports, where each player and their actions - no matter how small - is critical to the success of the entire team. A seatbelt violation may not seem like that big of a deal, but in fact, it can quickly result in 21 points being added to the Unsafe Driver category in no time. Although CSA scores are calculated monthly, the everyday decisions that individual driver makes - both on and off the road, significantly matters. CSA scores are closely related with Pre-Employment Screening Program (PSP) scores. This is the driver's individual rating, which the FMCSA maintains, and provides ‚Äúelectronic access to a commercial driver's five-year crash and three-year inspection history from the FMCSA Motor Carrier Management Information System (MCMIS).‚Äù Essentially, the inspections that count against (or for) the carrier also count against (or for) the driver‚Äôs PSP data. A driver can request a copy of his/her PSP score for a nominal fee. A carrier can get access to the individual score if the driver grants permission by signing a release, especially as part of the pre-employment process. Carriers that are focused on safety, such as TrueNorth, check a driver's PSP as part of the hiring process, and evaluate the driver's individual score against a certain threshold. Heath, Operations Manager at TrueNorth, tells us, ‚ÄúDrivers often don't realize that their cumulative CSA points that come from accidents and violations remain on their record for 3 years and the carrier's record for 2 years, even when that person leaves the fleet.‚Äù These points will have a direct impact on which companies will hire/contract them as well as which companies will continue to do business with that fleet. A carrier's CSA score is indicative of its fleet management and safety policies - yes. But it requires the buy-in, effort, and follow-through from every driver leased onto it for it to work. It's a full-contact sport. Your actions - whether you're a driver or fleet manager - matter in keeping yourself and everyone else safe. How Can You Improve Your CSA Score and Win? There are two ways to improve your CSA score by lowering it - minimizing violations and when peers‚Äô scores increase. First, minimizing violations. Having more good, clean inspections with no violations will drive the percentage of bad ones down. There are many things a fleet and a driver can do to work toward this. Fleets can implement a solid road safety plan, compliance training, and regular maintenance requirements. Drivers have the choice to always ensure compliance with the rules and regulations of the seven BASIC categories. For example, completing the pre- and post-trip inspections are critical in identifying and fixing issues before an inspector does. For details on ways to prepare for inspections, check out our article on CVSA Inspections . Many carriers reward clean inspections through financial incentives. At TrueNorth for example, any time a driver gets a clean inspection (no violations found), they receive a bonus. Depending on the inspection the driver receives, the bonus is $500 for a clean Level I, $250 for Level II, and $100 for Level III. Second, because a carrier's CSA score is a comparison with the scores of its peers (fleets of similar size), if other carriers do worse comparatively, then yours can improve automatically due to the movement of others. Finding and retaining your A-team cannot happen overnight. It takes a concerted effort - similar to training and coaching - to get there. If we all work together and try, we can not only win individual games, but we can make the playoffs and dominate the championships. Put us in, coach! Other relevant articles: DVIR: Pre-Trip and Post-Trip Inspections CVSA Inspections: Understanding and Preparing for Them How to Stay DOT Compliant

title: How to Stay Profitable During BFCM - Klaviyo
summary: Discover 12 expert-backed BFCM strategies to stay profitable, boost AOV, and protect margins, without relying on deep discounts, or sacrificing long-term growth.
body_text: Maximize BFCM profit margins Generated by Klaviyo AI The article explains how ecommerce brands can protect and grow contribution margin during Black Friday Cyber Monday by refining discounts, targeting high-value customers, and optimizing ad spend. It also covers tactics to reduce returns, improve post-purchase experiences, and re-engage BFCM shoppers for long-term profitability. Focus on contribution margin: Evaluate every BFCM tactic by whether it increases contribution margin after product, shipping, payment, returns, and media costs—not just top-line revenue. Segment high-value customers: Use customer segmentation to identify VIPs and high-LTV shoppers, then offer tailored perks like early access, exclusive launches, or personalized bundles to protect margins. Boost AOV with up- and cross-sells: Increase average order value through on-site recommendations, cart pop-ups, order-editing tools, and well-timed email, SMS, and ad-based cross-sell flows. Optimize ads for profit: Prioritize profit on ad spend by promoting high-margin products and building targeted audiences based on CLV and high-intent behaviors. Retain and re-engage buyers: Use post-purchase flows, tailored follow-up campaigns, and feedback surveys to reduce returns, prevent churn, and turn BFCM shoppers into repeat customers. Sign up Get a demo Staying profitable during Black Friday Cyber Monday is a balancing act. This year, economic uncertainty is keeping brands on their toes—and making it a good time to focus on resiliency. While BFCM is one of the best times to boost sales and acquire new customers, the key to long-term success lies in not just increasing revenue, but also maintaining healthy profits throughout this high-stakes shopping season. Remember: BFCM is not a revenue contest. It’s a contribution-margin contest. And contribution margin is not a number you can read off your dashboard the morning after Cyber Monday. Your November scoreboard is provisional. The real number lands in January, once returns clear, refunds leave your account, support tickets close, and the post-sale slowdown plays out. Plan for the settled number, not the spike. Of course, BFCM success is easier said than done. I’m the founder of Polaris Growth , where we’ve helped more than 80 ecommerce brands use Klaviyo to optimize their marketing efforts. And each year, I see opportunities for businesses to increase growth and profitability during this short but peak shopping season. For every tactic in this guide, use this one-line check: does it raise contribution margin after cost of goods sold, shipping, payment fees, expected returns, and media? If not, don’t run it. 1. Offer profit-friendly incentives Intense discounts can put a squeeze on your margins during BFCM. But it doesn’t have to be that way. Here are some ways to create value for customers without sacrificing a good chunk of your profits. 1. Bundle products Before you decide how to discount, decide what to discount. Putting your best full-price sellers on sale just hands margin to customers who were going to buy anyway. That’s the pull-forward trap: you move a future full-price sale into a discounted window and call it growth. Save your deepest cuts for overstock and slow movers, and protect your heroes. This approach involves combining multiple products into a single package deal, at a price that’s slightly lower than buying each item separately. Customers feel they’re getting more for their money—even if the discount per item is modest. By carefully selecting which products to bundle , you protect your overall margins. 2. Implement tiered discounts For instance, you can offer 10% off orders over $50, 15% off orders over $100, and 20% off orders over $150. This approach incentivizes customers to add more items to their cart to reach the next discount tier, boosting your overall average order value (AOV). 3. Offer free gifts with purchase Instead of discounts, you can offer customers a sample-sized product, a branded accessory, or a limited-edition item. The perceived value of a free gift often outweighs its cost to you, making this a great way to attract customers without significantly impacting your margins. “Tiered free gifts are one of the few BFCM incentives that let you create perceived value without putting your margins through the meat grinder,” says Ben Zettler, founder of Zettler Digital . “Choose gifts that are high impact for the customer, low cost for you, and aligned with what you want to move.” “This is also a smart way to clear out slow-moving inventory, as long as each tier feels intentional,” Zettler adds. “Position the gifts as exclusive, not just leftovers. That way, your AOV climbs and your profit doesn’t get torched.” Tiered free gifts are one of the few BFCM incentives that let you create perceived value without putting your margins through the meat grinder. Ben Zettler Founder, Zettler Digital 4. Run early-access deals Consider running unique, limited early-access deals. If you bake in a higher margin, and the segment properly, the sale can feel like a win for the shopper without you eroding your margins.Black Friday profit pro tip: Send this deal to subscribers who have been on your list for 3+ months but haven’t purchased yet. 2. Tailor your marketing to high-value segments I’m a big fan of using Klaviyo’s customer segmentation because it’s a high-impact, low-effort way to protect your margins. One of my favorite use cases around BFCM is to create segments for VIP customers based on their spending habits or purchase frequency. There are 3 primary approaches to take when deciding who your VIP customers are: Segment Approach 1. Big spenders Identify customers who have spent over a certain amount in the last 365 days. 2. Frequent purchasers Send to customers who have made a specific number of purchases in the last 365 days. 3. Blended approach Combine spending and frequency thresholds to capture your most valuable customers. Once you’ve identified your VIPs, you can nurture these relationships with exclusive offers, early access to BFCM sales , or personalized bundles. “Some brands make the mistake of blasting the same BFCM offer to everyone,” says Zettler. “While BFCM often means discount offers are involved, not every customer is a bargain shopper. Segmentation lets you invite loyalists and high-LTV customers to exclusive product launches instead of just giving them a coupon. You can deepen your loyalty and keep your margins intact.” 3. Take advantage of opportunities to up- and cross-sell When people are already shopping in your store or on your website during BFCM, there’s an opportunity to boost your AOV via up- and cross-selling. One way to do this is by providing on-site recommendations for related or upgraded products. For example, if you’re a footwear brand and a customer is browsing for running shoes, you can display a section titled “Complete Your Running Gear”, featuring moisture-wicking socks, running shorts, and a water bottle. You can even position these as stocking stuffers to spark gift ideas for customers. For carts that have a high AOV, consider putting a Klaviyo pop-up on the cart with lower-cost impulse purchase products. This can help you to increase a bit of AOV. You can also use integrations like OrderEditing that allow people to make changes to their order before it ships, without having to directly contact customer support. But even after a customer completes a purchase, there's an opportunity to capture more revenue. I encourage my clients to implement up- or cross-sell email flows to follow up after a purchase—whether that’s by sending personalized recommendations a few weeks after BFCM, or offering a one-time special deal on a related product immediately after the purchase. Ashley Ismailovski, director of email marketing at SmartSites , uses Klaviyo AI to send cross-sell messages at exactly the right time for each individual customer. In the product analysis dashboard , “use the ‘next best cross-sell date’ flow trigger to send an email to a customer when Klaviyo’s predictive analytics model has determined they would be most receptive to a cross-sell promotion,” she advises. “If you want to take it a step further,” Ismailovski says, “you can also use the ‘next best product’ block in your message to show the customer personalized product recommendations based on their previous purchases.” Use the 'next best product' block in your message to show the customer personalized product recs based on their previous purchase. Ashley Ismailovski Director of email marketing, SmartSites Customer Agent can also play a meaningful role in cross-sell during BFCM. When a shopper hesitates at checkout or abandons a cart, Customer Agent can step in (across web chat, SMS, or email) to answer fit or product questions, surface relevant recommendations based on browsing and purchase history, and guide the customer toward completing the purchase. It runs 24/7, which matters during a weekend when your team can't be everywhere at once.Updating Customer Agent’s knowledge around BFCM and your specific BFCM deals gives it the context it needs to help drive those sales while also providing value to your shoppers. Black Friday profit pro tip: If you have different deals for different segments, you can also configure this for the Customer Agent. That way, it knows who your VIPs are as opposed to your zero order shoppers, and can offer them deals accordingly. 4. Lean on your highest-margin channel The cheapest revenue you will earn all week comes through email and SMS, because there’s no media cost attached to it. Paid, meanwhile, is at its most expensive during BFCM, when every brand is bidding for the same impressions. That gap is why your owned channels do more for your margin in this one week than at any other time of year. My default is to send more than feels comfortable: if you planned one email, send two or three. Under-sending the inbox you already own, while paying peak prices for paid, is the more expensive mistake. The catch is that volume is only safe if you scale your exclusions with it. Test and ramp before BFCM. Do not jump from one send a week to several a day overnight, or you will trip provider throttling and tank your reputation right when it matters. Cut the dead weight first. Re-engage or suppress chronically unengaged profiles and remove bouncing addresses before the rush, not during it. Watch deliverability by provider. Klaviyo's deliverability reporting shows which inbox providers are flagging you. If Gmail or Outlook is struggling, drop to engaged-only on that provider rather than slowing every send down. Give people an exit that is not the spam button. Send a pre-BFCM email, or add a preference link, that lets subscribers opt out of your Black Friday sends specifically. The ones who self-select out would otherwise have reported you as spam. Google sets an explicit limit: keep spam complaints under 0.3%, and ideally under 0.1%. Yahoo now surfaces effectively the same thresholds in its Sender Hub. Since late 2025, Google also rejects non-compliant bulk mail outright rather than quietly filtering it, so everything above is how you push volume hard without crossing that line.Everything above is how you push volume hard without crossing that line. Black Friday profit pro tip : The brands that win the inbox during BFCM are not the ones who send the least to stay safe. They are the ones who send the most to a list they aggressively monitor and segment during this period. 5. Optimize for profit on ad spend Make every ad dollar count during BFCM by optimizing for profit on ad spend (POAS) rather than just return on ad spend (ROAS). While ROAS measures the gross revenue generated for every dollar spent on advertising, POAS takes into account your profit margins. So even though a campaign with a 4x ROAS might seem successful, your POAS may show otherwise. This is especially important during BFCM when many businesses offer significant discounts. POAS also factors in costs like shipping, payment processing fees, and product costs, which can fluctuate during high-volume sales periods like BFCM. To optimize your POAS, focus on advertising high-margin products. While the definition of a high margin will depend on the industry, in general I’d encourage brands to focus on the top 20% most profitable products that they’re selling. A POAS nuance worth flagging: a customer you acquire on a deep discount won’t necessarily repeat the same way a full-price customer does. The research is mixed, but, in my experience, deep-discount cohorts often repeat at lower rates, and many holiday buyers are gift-givers or one-time seasonal shoppers who were never likely to return. So, judge BFCM acquisition on expected lifetime value and second-purchase rate, not first-order ROAS. The brands that win BFCM are not the ones with the biggest November, they are the ones who turn one-time holiday buyers into a profitable second purchase in Q1. You can also utilize CLV in your CRM strategy. Again, I like to use Klaviyo’s segmentation to create highly targeted audiences for BFCM ads, such as a lookalike audience based on the highest-CLV customers. Jemma Sears, digital marketing manager at Kulani Kinis , a swimwear brand based in Australia, uses Klaviyo’s integration with Meta and Klaviyo Audience Sync to personalize paid ads to show the exact print a shopper subscribed to a back-in-stock notification for. “This is an effective way to leverage demand with a high-intent audience,” Sears shares. “We saw a reduced cost per acquisition with this audience compared to our typical remarketing audiences. It was over $10 cheaper to convert our Klaviyo audiences—quite compelling when you look at scaling this strategy.” 6. Turn expensive holiday traffic into owned contacts During BFCM you’re paying peak prices to bring visitors to your site, and most of them won’t buy on the first visit. Anyone who leaves without giving you an email address or phone number is gone, and you will pay that same peak price to reach them again. So treat data capture as a margin lever, not a list-building nicety. A well-targeted sign-up form, an exit-intent offer, or a short quiz turns an expensive one-time visitor into an owned contact you can sell to at almost no marginal cost for months. That is how a peak-CAC customer can become profitable: the full-margin purchase often shows up in Q1, not on Black Friday. Capture a preference or two, such as category or size, so your January follow-up is relevant rather than generic. 7. Avoid promoting high-return products One easy way to minimize costly returns is to avoid heavy promotion of products with high return rates. While the National Retail Federation (NRF) found returns in 2025 were down by about 1% from 2024, return rates can vary significantly depending on the industry. Use benchmark data to gauge whether the rates for a certain product are considered high. Or, if you have access to your BFCM data from last year, use that to identify which of your products had the highest return rates. The main problem you’re trying to prevent is promoting products that, on average, have the highest return rate in your assortment. While many factors can impact returns, you want to minimize the chances of paying top dollar to get people to your shop—only to create even more work and costs for your team because you chose to market the wrong product. Here are some ways to manage the problem of high returns around BFCM: Build a returns reserve into your profit and loss statement. Cap discounts on historically high-return categories. Put a lower ceiling on discounts for categories with above-average return rates. Promote bundles and add-ons for those categories to raise perceived value without deep cuts. When returns hit matters as much as how many. The revenue you book in November starts coming back in late December and January, and extended holiday windows push some of it even later. That creates three problems: revenue gets clawed back weeks after you celebrated it, cash leaves your account after you have already paid for product, shipping, and fees, and support gets buried exactly when it is most thinly staffed. Plan for all three: hold a returns reserve, staff or deflect the January support wave, and use your post-purchase flow to set sizing and usage expectations so fewer orders come back at all.Returns will always cost businesses money, but these tactics will better protect your profits and ensure a better customer experience. 8. Promote profitable payment and shipping methods While most brands focus on the shopping experience, it’s equally important to pay attention to what comes after: payment and shipping. Here are two ways to guide customers toward options that benefit your bottom line: 1. Offer payment methods with lower processing fees Different payment methods come with varying transaction costs for your business. Find ways to nudge customers toward the lower-fee options. For instance, you can offer a small discount for using certain payment methods. To figure out how much of a discount to offer, start by comparing payment methods and measuring the difference between those options. The goal, of course, is to promote the cheaper alternative for your business. Keep in mind that returns may have additional handling costs as well. Black Friday profit pro tip: For the European Union, make sure you adhere to regulations . 2. Provide cost-effective shipping optionsConsider providing free shipping with minimum order values set above the AOV, which can increase average order size while keeping shipping costs manageable.You can also look at the cost of each shipment carrier and promote the cheapest options, while adding a small fee for the more expensive ones. 9. Prevent buyer’s remorse Reduce returns and build customer satisfaction by implementing post-purchase email flows that reinforce the value of people’s BFCM purchases. A few ideas: Send a celebratory “Your order is on the way” email after the package ships to build excitement. Share usage or educational tips for the product someone purchased to help them get the most value out of it. Showcase user-generated content featuring the product a customer purchased for inspiration. Customer Agent can also support this goal directly. When a customer reaches out post-purchase with a question (about sizing, usage, or returns) Agent resolves it immediately, with full context from their order history and profile, without your team having to step in. That kind of fast, informed response does more to prevent remorse than almost any follow-up email. For brands running Customer Hub, the post-purchase experience extends to the website itself — giving every logged-in customer a personalized view of their orders, loyalty rewards, and product recommendations the moment they return to your site. Also make sure you think about who you’re excluding from each campaign send. There’s nothing that frustrates a customer more than receiving an email about bigger discounts or price drops 24 hours after they placed their order at a higher price. Black Friday profit pro tip: When a return is unavoidable, treat it as a second chance to sell, not just a loss to process. A refund reverses the revenue and sends cash out the door. An exchange or store credit keeps the revenue on your books and the cash in your business, and it keeps the customer. Platforms like Loop Returns and AfterShip make instant exchanges and bonus credit the default path. One caution: incentivize the exchange, but don’t trap people into it. NRF found that 57% of shoppers won’t buy from a retailer again after being charged for a return. 10. Give back to a good cause Consider donating a portion of your BFCM profits to a charity that aligns with your brand values. If you sell outdoor gear, for instance, you might partner with an environmental conservation organization. You can then create a special BFCM collection where a higher percentage of sales goes to charity, or offer customers the option to round up their purchase to the nearest dollar for donation. This approach not only contributes to a good cause, but can also account for premium pricing and attract customers who want their purchases to make a positive impact. Just ask London Sock Co. When the brand donated two pairs of socks to a homeless charity for every purchase during BFCM, the strategy contributed to a 180% increase in AOV during the sale period. 11. Re-engage customers post-BFCM Don’t let your BFCM customers disappear after the holidays. Here are a few ideas to re-engage customers after the holiday rush dies down: 1. Implement robust follow-up marketing campaigns With Klaviyo, you can tailor your messages based on purchase history and LTV. For instance, create a segment of first-time BFCM buyers and send them a welcome series that introduces your brand story, showcases your bestselling products, and offers a small incentive for their next purchase. George Rodríguez, founder of A-Game Digital , recommends compressing the typical 30-day sales window after BFCM. “We’re creating time pressure and telling customers, ‘If you know you’ll need this item again, grab it soon instead of waiting,'” he explains. Here’s how Rodríguez’s team at A-Game approaches this: Use marketing analytics to identify products with strong repeat buying patterns or natural cross-sell potential. Develop time-sensitive messaging emphasizing the brief availability of winter holiday promotions. Highlight complementary products that work well together with customers’ original selections. Klaviyo Composer makes this re-engagement execution faster. Rather than rebuilding campaigns from scratch for each post-BFCM segment, you can brief Composer on the audience and goal — 'first-time BFCM buyers, 30-day follow-up, introduce the brand, soft incentive for second purchase' — and get a coordinated email and SMS campaign ready to review in minutes. The output is informed by how that segment has engaged so far, so the messaging starts from a relevant place rather than a blank page. We’re creating time pressure and telling customers, ‘If you know you’ll need this item again, grab it soon instead of waiting' George Rodríguez Founder, A-Game Digital 2. Don’t forget about your existing customers After BFCM, send existing customers personalized product recommendations based on their recent buys, or create an exclusive “loyal customer” offer for the new year. Rodríguez suggests personalizing the follow-up offer based on the customer’s RFM segment. “If it’s a new customer in the ‘Recent’ segment, use language that acknowledges their current status in the lifecycle and highlight what most customers buy next,” he advises. “And be sure to emphasize that they’re getting a deal due to the holiday.”“If they’re a ‘Champion’ customer, thank them for their loyalty and present the offer graciously,” Rodríguez adds. “If they’ve churned, welcome them back and thank them with a follow-up offer they can use now or share with friends and family.” 3. Find out how your customers experienced shopping with you A post-purchase survey is a great way to gather feedback and improve future campaigns, while also keeping your brand top of mind for customers. If you use Klaviyo Customer Hub , the “Service interactions”section will show you which self-service support interactions your customers have taken. This can help you find weak spots in your customer journey so you can improve future experiences. Tracked service interactions include: Orders tracked Returns started Coupons applied Clicks on the help buttons Web chat conversations started By focusing on these post-BFCM engagement strategies, you can turn one-time holiday shoppers into year-round revenue drivers, maximizing the long-term value of your BFCM efforts. Customer Agent also feeds this loop. Every conversation it resolves captures signals about what customers asked, what they struggled with, and what they wanted — and that data enriches the customer profile automatically. Over time, those signals sharpen your segmentation and make your post-BFCM campaigns more relevant for the following year. 12. Lower your winback and acquisition costs with direct mail Direct mail sits outside the ad auction, so its cost stays fixed while paid prices spike through BFCM. In certain cases that makes it the cheaper way to reach a customer, since a postcard can cost less than serving someone ads at peak-season prices, especially people who are expensive to reach with paid but cheap to reach by mail. It is also the only owned channel that still reaches customers who have stopped opening your email or unsubscribed, the ones your biggest send of the year never lands with. Two ways I use it during BFCM: Inbox backup: mail a postcard to subscribers who did not open your sale email. Retargeting layer: trigger postcards for cart and checkout abandoners. On Klaviyo, you can fire these from inside your existing flows. Two things to plan for: Lead time: you commit print and postage weeks ahead, so this is an October decision, not a Black Friday one. Measurement: judge it on incremental ROAS against a holdout. That is the only number that proves the channel paid for itself. PostPilot , Klaviyo's premier direct mail partner, reports postcards starting around $0.55 including postage and median incremental ROAS over BFCM of roughly 3.5x to 5.8x depending on size, strongest on winback and retention rather than cold prospecting. Use these strategies to protect your hard-earned BFCM profits I’ve seen firsthand how these strategies can help brands keep more money in their pockets during and after the holiday season. Start planning to implement these strategies right now to help make your BFCM as profitable as possible. Omar Lovert As CEO & founder of Polaris Growth, a Klaviyo Elite agency in the Netherlands, Omar Lovert helps ecommerce brands in the USA, Canada, the Netherlands, and across Europe grow with lifecycle strategy, Klaviyo, CRO, and customer lifetime value optimization. He’s the first and only official Klaviyo Legend, an original Klaviyo Champion, and co-host of the Klaviyo Geeks podcast. title: Email Deliverability Services: A Complete Guide for 2026
summary: Learn how email deliverability services improve inbox placement and sender reputation. Compare top platforms to find the best fit.
body_text: Email deliverability services help senders improve inbox placement through authentication management, sender reputation building, warmup automation, inbox placement monitoring, and deliverability analytics. A recent Validity benchmark found that 84.8% of messages reached the inbox globally, while 6.1% landed in spam and 9.1% went missing , meaning roughly 1 in 6 emails failed to reach the inbox even before content, targeting, or reputation were considered ( Validity's 2025 benchmark report ). That gap explains why a simple warmup tool isn't always enough. Basic tools automate sending activity, while a full deliverability service connects engagement, authentication, provider-level monitoring, list hygiene, and expert diagnosis into one operating system for email. Why Email Deliverability Services Exist A campaign can report strong delivery while producing weak visibility because accepted messages may still miss the inbox. Inbox placement tracks what happens after a receiving provider accepts the message: it may reach the inbox, enter spam, or disappear into another filtering layer. That distinction matters because delivery reports alone cannot show whether recipients can see a campaign ( Mailjet's explanation of inbox placement ). The commercial impact is significant. Global inbox placement stands at 84.8% , while 6.1% of messages reach spam and 9.1% go missing, according to Validity's 2025 benchmark report . Senders therefore lose part of their audience before copy, segmentation, or conversion strategy can affect results. At scale, small changes influence large volumes across Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, and other providers. What the category actually includes Email deliverability consulting services include platforms, consultants, and software-and-expert teams that improve the conditions affecting inbox placement. That can include software-led platforms, in-house deliverability teams, and specialist consulting providers such as MailAdept , which focuses on email deliverability consulting. Their work typically covers: Authentication management: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC setup, alignment checks, reporting, and policy enforcement. Reputation management: Monitoring sender behavior, complaints, bounces, and engagement signals. Warmup automation: Generating controlled interactions to establish or rebuild sending reputation. Inbox placement monitoring: Testing message placement across specific mailbox providers. Deliverability analytics: Connecting technical issues with campaign and sender-level outcomes. Expert guidance: Diagnosing problems that dashboards cannot explain. Authentication configured in DNS does not guarantee that a sender is enforcing it. A warmup tool may exchange messages or automate opens, yet leave a misaligned DMARC policy, provider-specific filtering, or uneven Gmail and Outlook performance undetected. A basic warmup tool can suit a lightly used mailbox with clean authentication and modest sending. A fuller service fits teams scaling outreach, managing several domains, sending marketing campaigns, serving multiple clients, or recovering from spam placement. The trade-off is straightforward: warmup automates one behavior, while broader services add monitoring, diagnosis, and provider-specific controls. Core Features of Email Deliverability Services A strong service doesn't treat warmup as the whole solution. It combines several controls because inbox providers evaluate technical identity, sending behavior, recipient response, and reputation together. Warmup automation Warmup should create realistic engagement signals, not just a rising send count. Useful activity can include opens, replies, conversation threads, spam removal, and marking messages as important. Provider-level controls matter because a sender may perform well with Gmail while struggling with Outlook or Microsoft 365. Warmup also needs restraint. Artificially increasing volume without monitoring complaints, bounces, or authentication can make a weak sending system appear active without making it trustworthy. Authentication management SPF identifies authorized sending servers. DKIM helps prove that a message wasn't altered in transit. DMARC applies a policy when SPF or DKIM checks fail and provides reporting visibility. Microsoft's authentication guidance explains these roles, while NIST notes that DMARC can pass when either SPF or DKIM succeeds and aligns with the visible From domain ( Microsoft's email authentication guidance ). The practical issue is coordination. A company may have several sending platforms, forms, CRMs, and outbound tools. Each source must preserve alignment, or legitimate messages can fail policy even when individual records exist. Testing, analytics, and list cleaning Inbox placement testing shows where accepted messages land. Analytics then connect those results with spam complaints, reputation indicators, bounces, and engagement. List cleaning removes risky or inactive recipients before they continue damaging sender signals. Teams that also manage customer communication may find operational guidance useful, including this resource on boosting business with CallZent email support . The same principle applies to deliverability: reliable processes matter more than isolated sending activity. Expert support A specialist can distinguish a content issue from an authentication issue, a provider-specific reputation problem, or a list-quality failure. That diagnosis prevents teams from repeatedly changing subject lines when the problem sits in DNS alignment or complaint handling. Practical rule: Warmup activity without authentication, monitoring, and list hygiene is incomplete deliverability work. The Authentication Enforcement Gap SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records establish identity, but inbox protection depends on how consistently those controls are enforced. Teams often leave DMARC in monitoring mode while sending platforms, domains, and provider rules change around it. DMARC adoption has grown faster than enforcement. Mailgun's 2025 State of Email Deliverability report found that 53.8% of senders used DMARC in 2024, up from 42.6% in 2023 , while only 25.5% of DMARC users planned to enforce a stricter policy that year. It also reported that only 13% of senders used inbox placement testing ( Mailgun's 2025 State of Email Deliverability report ). Why configured doesn't mean protected Authentication can fail operationally even when DNS records exist. Review these failure points: A third-party sender is missing from SPF authorization. DKIM signs with a domain that does not align with the visible From domain. A newly added platform sends mail outside the authentication plan. DMARC reports are not reviewed, leaving legitimate failures undiagnosed. A policy remains in observation mode instead of progressing toward Quarantine or Reject. The practical work is maintaining alignment across every sending source. A CRM, form, outbound tool, or marketing platform can introduce a failure after the original setup is complete. Teams also need a defined process for reviewing reports, approving new senders, and responding to unauthorized traffic. Provider rules are operational requirements Gmail may mark unauthenticated messages as spam or reject them with a 5.7.26 error . Since February 2024, senders delivering 5,000 or more messages per day to Gmail accounts must authenticate outgoing email, avoid unwanted or unsolicited messages, and provide a clear unsubscribe option, according to Gmail's sender guidelines . Relevant implementations also require SPF, DKIM, DMARC, one-click list-unsubscribe, and valid reverse and forward DNS under Google's bulk-sender requirements . A practical process for avoiding the spam folder therefore includes policy enforcement, alignment checks, report review, and provider-specific monitoring. Basic warmup tools can help establish sending history, while full-service platforms are better suited to managing multiple sources and ongoing enforcement. Deliverability Needs by Sender Type Sender type determines which reputation risks deserve attention first. Sales teams sending personalized outreach need controlled warmup, realistic engagement, and complaint protection. Marketing teams need testing, segmentation, and list hygiene. High-volume senders must meet stricter provider requirements while enforcing consistent controls across every sending source. Google and Yahoo guidance sets a spam complaint limit below 0.30% , while industry guidance identifies 0.10% as a safer operating target ( bulk-sender deliverability guidance ). Audience quality and unsubscribe handling therefore affect deliverability directly. They are operating controls, not secondary campaign details. Deliverability Requirements by Sender Type Sender Type Primary Challenge Critical Features Volume Considerations Sales outreach teams Building reputation without generating unwanted-mail complaints Provider-level warmup, realistic replies, bounce prevention, complaint monitoring Increase sending cautiously and separate domains or streams where appropriate Marketing teams Maintaining engagement across campaigns and segments Inbox placement testing, list cleaning, spam score monitoring, analytics Segment audiences and suppress risky or inactive recipients High-volume senders Meeting layered provider requirements at scale SPF, DKIM, DMARC enforcement, one-click unsubscribe, reporting, provider monitoring Apply the Gmail requirements discussed earlier to Gmail-bound volume Recruitment agencies Managing mixed recipient and provider environments B2B warmup, provider-specific testing, content controls, reputation monitoring Keep recruiter, client, and marketing streams distinguishable B2B companies Uneven performance across Gmail, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Provider-level warmup, placement insights, authentication checks, expert review Avoid assuming one provider's results represent the whole audience Outlook and Office365 can behave differently from Gmail, particularly in mixed B2B environments. Benchmark coverage reports provider-level variation, including weaker performance for some Outlook, Hotmail, and Office365 segments ( B2B deliverability benchmark coverage ). A single warmup schedule cannot account for those differences. Sales outreach may need gradual volume control and reply monitoring, while marketing programs need stronger suppression and campaign-level testing. High-volume operations also need authentication enforcement and report review across each sending source, not merely a completed DNS setup. The right service should identify where reputation is weak, then let the sender adjust volume, engagement, and monitoring by provider. Basic warmup tools can support sending-history development. Full-service platforms are more suitable when several domains, providers, or sending systems require ongoing oversight. How to Evaluate Email Deliverability Services Start by asking whether the service explains and improves real inbox placement, not just how many emails it sends. A useful evaluation connects warmup activity with provider behavior, authentication status, reputation, and the reasons messages are filtered. Examine the network first. Aged, real inboxes can produce more meaningful engagement signals than newly created or obviously artificial accounts. The provider should explain how its network operates, which interactions it generates, and how senders can control the warmup profile. Six practical buying criteria Network quality: Look for aged real inboxes distributed across the providers that matter to the sender's audience. Signal realism: Check for replies, threads, opens, spam removal, and important marking, rather than automated opens alone. Provider control: Confirm that Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, and other relevant destinations can be monitored or targeted separately. Authentication depth: The platform should identify SPF, DKIM, and DMARC problems, including alignment failures and policies that are configured but not enforced. Reporting clarity: Reports should distinguish delivery from inbox placement and show reputation, spam score, bounces, and provider-level outcomes. Human support: Specialists should help when the evidence points to a DNS, content, list, or provider-policy problem. Red flags worth rejecting Avoid services that guarantee inbox placement. Mailbox providers make independent filtering decisions, and sender behavior can change results after a warmup program begins. Other warning signs include: Private inbox access: IMAP access or permission to read a user's inbox creates unnecessary security concerns. No authentication tools: Warmup cannot correct broken alignment or unmanaged sending sources. No provider detail: A blended score can conceal weak Outlook or Gmail performance. Activity without diagnosis: More automated sending does not explain why messages are filtered. No expert access: Self-service dashboards leave complex enforcement and reputation problems unresolved. Authentication deserves particular scrutiny. A completed DNS setup does not prove that every sending source is aligned, authorized, and subject to the intended DMARC policy. Check whether the service can expose those gaps and help teams enforce the policy across transactional, marketing, and sales systems. Teams comparing low-cost options can review Mailwarm's free email deliverability tools before deciding whether a broader platform is justified. Premium pricing makes sense when it covers real engagement, monitoring, authentication support, reputation protection, and specialist access, rather than send automation alone. A lower subscription price is not a saving if the service cannot show where messages land or why providers distrust them. How Mailwarm Approaches Deliverability Mailwarm was built for teams that treat inbox placement as a system, not a checkbox. Its product positioning combines warmup with monitoring, authentication support, provider-level controls, and access to deliverability specialists. That broader scope explains why it is evaluated differently from a basic warmup utility. The implementation choice that matters most is separation by provider. Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, and SMTP environments can produce different results for the same sender. Mailwarm lets teams examine and direct activity by provider, so a weak Outlook result does not disappear inside one blended score. Security also affects the buying decision.
